title: LightThinker: Thinking Step-by-Step Compression
one_line_claim: Dynamically compresses intermediate reasoning steps in LLMs by training models to encode verbose thoughts into compact token representations, reducing peak memory and inference time while maintaining accuracy.
method_summary: LightThinker trains LLMs to dynamically compress intermediate reasoning (chain-of-thought) steps by converting verbose thought sequences into compact representations using gist tokens, while preserving critical reasoning via thought-based attention masks. Input is the reasoning chain; mechanism involves data reconstruction with special compression tokens and specialized attention masks; output is compressed reasoning enabling subsequent generation.

key_findings.finding: LightThinker reduces peak token usage by 70% on Qwen and Llama while maintaining competitive accuracy
key_findings.quote: on the Qwen, LightThinker sacrifices 1% accuracy but saves 26% time, reduces the peak tokens by 70%, and decreases Dep. by 78% (i.e., achieves a 16.6/3.7=4.5x compression ratio).

key_findings.finding: LightThinker reduces inference time by an average of 52% on Qwen and 41% on Llama under same memory constraints
key_findings.quote: LightThinker (rho.) achieves similar performance with lower Dep values (i.e., similar compression rate) while reducing inference time by an average of 52% on Qwen and 41% on Llama.

key_findings.finding: Introduces Dependency (Dep) metric to quantify compression degree, measuring reliance on historical tokens during generation
key_findings.quote: we introduce the Dependency (Dep) metric, defined as the total number of historical tokens each generated token depends on

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression efficiency, evaluate compression via accuracy retention and memory/compute metrics, and consider compression applied during reasoning-task generation.
differs_on: LightThinker trains the generator itself to perform lossy compression of reasoning; HERALD treats the compressor as a black box and predicts failures post-hoc from logit signals.
LightThinker compresses intermediate thoughts deliberately for efficiency; HERALD detects catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) triggered by external compression algorithms.
LightThinker measures compression via Dependency metric (information retention); HERALD measures failure via token-level logit anomalies as time series.
